status: CANDIDATE — locks after the first accepted render, exactly as Crystal Bears' did
_law: Injected verbatim into every emission. Never paraphrased, never hand-tuned mid-production. Brand names (Hilda, Gravity Falls, Over the Garden Wall) live in the bible for humans and NEVER appear in emissions — brand_block rule, paid for by Crystal Bears renders.
_v101_change: 2026-08-13, director's call. v1.0.0's background clause named Victorian arcade interiors specifically, so it could not be injected verbatim into a workshop, a street or an 1867 atelier — the first emission silently rewrote it, which breaks the verbatim law. The base text is now location-neutral; location colour moves to location_clauses and is appended, verbatim, after the base text when that location is in frame. Nothing about the look changed.
text: Hand-drawn 2D animation. Warm coloured-ink linework in browns, ambers and muted greens — never black outlines. Flat colour fills with a subtle paper texture, as if painted on lightly grained stock. Soft amber-warm palette with honeyed light. Characters are simple, expressive shapes with large readable eyes and distinctive silhouettes; their movement is gentle and slightly springy, drawn on twos. Backgrounds are richly detailed painted interiors rendered flat with painted depth, no perspective tricks. Cosy storybook atmosphere with quiet melancholy underneath. No 3D rendering, no photorealism, no painterly brushwork, no cel-shine gradients.

location_clauses.arcade: The arcade is Victorian: ornate ironwork, tiled floors and glass roof light, rendered flat.
location_clauses.workshop: The workshop is a working restorer's room: worn timber, brass and tools, lit by one bench lamp with cool daylight from a brick window.
location_clauses.burgundy_1867: Burgundy in 1867: cream-and-ochre stone, terracotta roofs, plane-tree shade, late-summer light low and honeyed.

_negatives_note: These are declared STYLE, not generic boilerplate — they define what the show's look is not, and sd25-pe principle 8 forbids only unrequested boilerplate. Watermark/subtitle/text-in-frame negatives were REMOVED 2026-08-13: principle 8 names them explicitly, and they cost prompt budget for nothing.
palette_law: Amber-warm inside the arcade and shop, always. Each historical destination gets its OWN locked palette, declared per episode before its first render.
